articles.headline: How top 2027 women's basketball commits fit at their schools
articles.description: Breaking down Vanderbilt's highest-rated recruit since Mikayla Blakes, plus more recruiting analysis for 2027-28.

images.name: Haylen Ayers [1296x729]
images.caption: Haylen Ayers will play for her mother's alma mater, Vanderbilt, next season.

images.name: Micah Ojo [1296x729]
images.caption: Star wing Micah Ojo is the first commit of the 2027 recruiting cycle for North Carolina.

images.name: Sydney Savoury [1296x729]
images.caption: Sydney Savoury has committed to UConn.

images.name: Nation Williams [1296x729]
images.caption: Nation Williams has committed to UCLA.

images.name: Jayla Forbes, Vic Schaefer [1296x729]
images.caption: Five-star Jayla Forbes is the second-best post in the 2027 class -- and will fit perfectly into Texas' system in the 2027-28 season

images.caption: Miciah Fusilier is one of two five-stars in the SC Next 100 class of 2027 committed to Baylor.

images.name: Eve Long [1296x729]
images.caption: Five-star forward Eve Long has committed to Notre Dame.

images.name: Lauren Hassell [1296x729]
images.caption: Lauren Hassell, a top-10 recruit in the SC Next class of 2027, is the first commit of the cycle for Vanderbilt.

images.name: Ryan Carter [1296x729]
images.caption: Ryan Carter's commitment gives North Carolina a third straight year of recruiting five-star backcourt players.

images.name: Avery Arije [1290x726]
images.caption: Avery Arije is the third top 100 commitment for Notre Dame in the 2027 cycle.

images.name: Zaniya Johnson [1296x729]
images.caption: Zaniya Johnson is the third top-30 commit for South Carolina in the 2027 class.

images.caption: Qandace Samuels is the second five-star of the 2027 cycle to commit to Texas.
